chunks.title: Your account
chunks.text:
**Full legal name** — prints on signature blocks and productions, and names you
in every audit line.

**Job title** — shown to colleagues. Carries no authority of its own.

**State bar number** and **issued by**.

  The bar number is the important field. With it on file you may approve AI
  output and be made lead on a matter. Clearing it takes both away on your next
  request.

  Approval authority is **derived from the licence you record here**, not
  granted by a checkbox.

**Work email** — your sign-in address. Changing it has to be confirmed from the
mailbox that receives it, which is not wired up yet; ask an administrator.

chunks.title: Your account
chunks.text:
Every session, with the device and when it started.

- **Revoke** ends one.
- **Sign out everywhere else** ends all but this one.

Revoking takes effect on the next request from that device, not at its next
sign-in. A session you do not recognise should be revoked.

chunks.title: Your account
chunks.text:
Set it up, generate new backup codes, or turn it off — unless your firm requires
it, in which case it cannot be turned off here.

The flow: scan the code with any TOTP app, save the backup codes somewhere that
is **not** the phone you just enrolled, then confirm with a code from the app.
Your current password is asked for first, so that somebody at your unlocked
screen cannot attach their own authenticator to your account.

- A code is not asked for on a trusted device for thirty days.
- Backup codes work once each and are never shown again.
- Generating a new set invalidates the old one immediately.

See [Signing in](/start/signing-in) for the full detail.

chunks.title: Your account
chunks.text:
Shown, and not editable. *A role is granted by an administrator. Being able to
raise your own would make every other permission in the product decorative.*

chunks.title: Your account
chunks.text:
Three counts, and the distinction between them is the point:

**Matters you can open** — assigned to you and readable.

**Matters you lead** — the only person who may release anything on these.

**Matters you administer** — you know these exist and can manage the roster; you
cannot read the file.

  Ethical walls that apply to you are not listed here. A walled matter shows no
  trace anywhere, and a line saying you are walled off one would be the
  disclosure the wall exists to prevent.

chunks.title: Your account
chunks.text:
Which in-app notices also reach your inbox, at this firm: mentions, task
assignments, task due dates. Each firm you belong to has its own setting.

chunks.title: What the analysis reads
chunks.text:
Every analysis discloses its own coverage. The panel at the top of the Analysis
tab reads, for example, *31 read · 4 withheld*, and opening it accounts for
every document on the matter.

  Coverage is **disclosed, never chosen**. There is no per-run document picker.
  What the engine may read is decided by the flags on each document, and the
  panel tells you what that came to.

chunks.title: What the analysis reads
chunks.text:
| Bucket | Why | What it means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Read** | Text extracted. | Quotable, and cited in the findings. |
| **Privileged** | The privilege flag. | Never retrieved, never quoted, never produced. |
| **Work product** | The work-product flag. | The firm's own analysis. Never retrieved, never released. |
| **Withdrawn** | Taken off the matter. | The engine no longer opens it. |
| **No file behind it** | Recorded without a document to read. | Off a privilege log, or still uploading. |

chunks.title: What the analysis reads
chunks.text:
**Privilege and work product are excluded by the system itself. No role, grant
or setting turns them on.**

That is the entire mechanism. There is nothing to configure, so there is nothing
to misconfigure.

chunks.title: What the analysis reads
chunks.text:
Only one thing changes a document's bucket, and it is the document itself:

- Clear the **privileged** or **work product** flag on the document, and it
  becomes eligible on the next run.
- **Restore** a withdrawn document to the matter.
- Upload the file behind a document that was recorded without one.
- Ask for an unreadable document to be [read
  again](/documents/reading#reading-a-document-again).

chunks.title: What the analysis reads
chunks.text:
Two empty states you may hit on the Analysis tab:

**"Nothing has been filed on this matter yet."** File a document.

**"All 6 documents on this matter are withheld from the analysis."** Everything
present is privileged, work product, withdrawn, or has no file. The run refuses
rather than producing an empty analysis.

The same thing said at the moment you press Analyse: *There is nothing on this
matter the analysis may read.*

chunks.title: Developments and alerts
chunks.text:
The **What changed** section is the analysis's answer to *is this matter
different from last week*. Each development carries why it matters, the new
risks and opportunities it creates, and a recommended response.

Pick the window across the top:

- Since the last analysis
- Since the last upload
- Last 7 days · Last 30 days
- Since the last deposition
- Everything

  *Nothing material in this period* is a real answer, not an empty state. The
  record has grown and nothing in it moved the case — widen the window to see
  earlier developments.

chunks.title: Developments and alerts
chunks.text:
New supporting evidence · New harmful evidence · Contradictory testimony ·
Impeachment material · New witness · Missing evidence · New claim · Weakened
claim · New defense · Increased damages · Reduced damages · Procedural risk ·
Deadline · Settlement leverage · Trial strategy

Each development carries a **materiality**: critical, high, moderate, low or
informational — and a **confidence**: low, medium or high.

chunks.title: Developments and alerts
chunks.text:
Alerts are the subset that wants your attention now. They appear on the matter's
overview, on the Analysis tab, and on the dashboard.

| Kind | Raised when |
| --- | --- |
| Score moved | An overall or category score changed materially. |
| Witness contradicted | The record contradicts a witness. |
| Gap resolved | Something the analysis had asked for arrived. |
| Claim strength changed | |
| Procedural risk | |
| Deadline approaching | |
| Settlement value | |
| Action now urgent | A recommended action's priority rose. |
| Document problem | A document could not be read, or its date is unclear. |
| Impeachment material | |

Each is **New**, **Acknowledged**, **Dismissed** or **Resolved**. Acknowledging
one says you have seen it; dismissing one takes it off the list.

chunks.title: Developments and alerts
chunks.section: Choosing what you are told about
chunks.text:
**What you are told about**, on the Analysis tab, applies to **this matter
only**:

- **Alert me from** — the minimum severity that raises an alert at all.
- **Show alerts in the app**
- **Email me**
- **Mute this matter**

  Email carries the case number and the kind of development, never the facts.
  Nothing substantive about a matter is sent to an inbox.

Notifications about tasks and mentions are separate, and configured on
[Your account](/account).

chunks.title: Developments and alerts
chunks.text:
**Case evolution** lists every version of the analysis with what triggered it —
*after Deposition of R. Alvarez was read*, *started by hand*, *phase changed* —
who started it, whether it was full or incremental, and how it ended.

**Compare two versions** puts any two side by side and reports what moved
between them: developments, gaps opened, gaps closed, actions added.

chunks.title: Your facts
chunks.text:
The analysis reads documents. Some of what an attorney knows was never written
down — a call, a concession made in a corridor, a client's account of something
no record captures.

**Your facts**, on the Analysis tab, is where that goes. State one fact, as you
would to a colleague.

chunks.title: Your facts
chunks.text:
A fact you record is given to **every later analysis**. Adding one re-runs the
analysis, so the effect is immediate rather than waiting for the next document.

chunks.title: Your facts
chunks.text:
A **locked** fact is treated as **settled** rather than as something to re-test
against a document that appears to disagree with it.

  This is the difference that matters. An unlocked fact is one more input the
  engine weighs. A locked one is ground truth: if a document contradicts it, the
  document is the thing in question, not your fact.

Lock on the way in with **Lock as verified**, or lock and unlock afterwards.

chunks.title: Your facts
chunks.text:
A fact can be marked **excluded** — kept on the record, not given to runs. Use it
for something that turned out to be wrong, where deleting it would lose the
history of having believed it.

**Remove** deletes it outright.

chunks.title: Your facts
chunks.text:
They are different tools.

- A **fact** is a proposition. It has no date and is handed to every stage of
  every run.
- A **chronology event** is something that happened on a date. Adding one by
  hand is for what no document records — the call, the meeting with no minutes.

See [Chronology](/chronology).

chunks.title: Gaps, contradictions, actions
chunks.text:
What the analysis knows to ask for and cannot find on the file. Each gap says
**how to get it**.

Ten categories: missing document · missing testimony · missing damages support ·
missing causation evidence · missing policy or procedure · missing
communications · missing expert analysis · missing authentication · incomplete
discovery response · unresolved contradiction.

States: **Open**, **In progress**, **Resolved**, **Unavailable**, **No longer
relevant**.

A gap answered by a document that arrives later closes on its own, and the
product tells you which document did it — *Answered by Maintenance log
2019–2021*. Closed gaps are hidden by default; **Show closed** brings them back.

*No open gaps* means everything the analysis knows to ask for is on the file.

chunks.title: Gaps, contradictions, actions
chunks.text:
Two lists, from the same pass over the record.

**Contradictions** — where the record disagrees with itself. Each shows both
sides: *the record says* against *against*.

Types: inconsistent dates · conflicting statements · testimony against a
document · account changed.

**Corroboration** — where it agrees. Confirmed by witnesses · document
corroborates testimony. And the inverse, flagged as an *unsupported allegation*.

Each carries a state you set: **Open**, **Resolved**, **Explained**, **Still
disputed**.

chunks.title: Gaps, contradictions, actions
chunks.text:
What the analysis thinks should happen next, most urgent first, each with its
**expected impact**.

Twelve categories: discovery request · deposition question · witness follow-up ·
document request · expert consultation · motion strategy · settlement
preparation · damages development · credibility investigation · evidence
preservation · trial preparation · client follow-up.

Priority: critical, high, moderate, low.

chunks.title: Gaps, contradictions, actions
chunks.text:
**Make a task** puts it on the matter's task board, optionally assigned to
someone. The action then shows *on the board, assigned to …*.

Marking an action **complete** is one of the triggers that starts a fresh
analysis run — the point being that the run then re-reads the file with the
thing you did on it.

States: Open · In progress · Completed · Dismissed · Superseded.

chunks.title: Gaps, contradictions, actions
chunks.text:
A map of what supports what. Each link joins a piece of evidence to a target,
with a relation and a strength out of 100.

**Targets:** claim · defense · element · witness · damages · issue · score.

**Relations:** supports · contradicts · corroborates · impeaches · authenticates
· quantifies.

**Kinds of evidence:** direct · circumstantial · testimonial · documentary ·
expert · demonstrative.

  Everything here is reviewable the same way: approve, reject, mark incorrect,
  mark privileged, or suppress. A rejected finding is not raised again.

chunks.title: How the analysis works
chunks.text:
An **analysis run** reads the matter's documents and writes a numbered
**version**. Scores, developments, gaps, contradictions, actions and the memo
all hang off that version. Nothing is overwritten: v4 does not erase v3, and the
current analysis is simply the newest successful run.

chunks.title: How the analysis works
chunks.text:
The first analysis runs as soon as a document has been read. After that:

**Automatically**, when the file changes in a way that matters — a document
added, replaced or withdrawn; a deposition added; discovery received; damages
evidence added; a witness added; a ruling entered; a deadline changed; an
attorney recorded a fact; the claims changed; a recommended action completed;
the phase changed.

**By hand**, with **Analyse** / **Re-analyse** on the Analysis tab.

Attorneys, paralegals and firm owners can run an analysis. Only an attorney can
approve its output.

chunks.title: How the analysis works
chunks.text:
A run works through the file in order. Each stage writes its own row, and you
can watch them land one at a time.

| Stage | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Knowledge base** | The same party, spelled four ways, resolved. Parties, facts, timeline events and the evidence list every later stage cites into. |
| **Case summary** | States the matter neutrally. |
| **Research checklist** | The questions this matter raises. |
| **Analogous precedents** | Decisions that resemble this one. |
| **Legal research** | Authority for the questions asked. |
| **Theory and damages** | The theory, the damages model, the defences to expect. |
| **Scoring** | Prices the judgement already made. |
| **Memo** | The prose an attorney reads first. |
| **Developments** | What changed, and what to do about it. |

Grouped into five phases on the run review screen: ingest, frame and retrieve,
structure, score and decide, compose and commit.

chunks.title: How the analysis works
chunks.text:
Stages cite an **index into the evidence list**, never a quote they composed.
The index resolves back to the fact, the document and the page.

  This is the point: the worst a model can do is cite the wrong index, which
  points at a real passage that visibly does not support the claim. It cannot
  invent a passage that does not exist.

Every citation in the product shows the document and the page — *p. 14* — and
clicking it opens the document there.

chunks.title: How the analysis works
chunks.text:
| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Queued** | Not started. |
| **Running** | In progress. |
| **Complete** | Succeeded. |
| **Carried forward** | Nothing it depends on changed, so the previous run's result was reused. |
| **Skipped** | It could be skipped, and it was. |
| **Failed** | It did not finish. |

Some stages are **required**: if one fails, the run ends there. The rest are
**skippable**: the run carries on without them and the step records why. A run
where that happened is *Partly complete*.

chunks.title: How the analysis works
chunks.text:
Queued · Running · Complete · Partly complete · Failed · **No change** — the run
finished and found nothing that moved the matter.

chunks.title: How the analysis works
chunks.text:
A run is either **full** or **incremental**. An incremental run reuses what has
not changed and re-does what has, which is why a stage can show as *carried
forward from run 6*.

chunks.title: How the analysis works
chunks.text:
If every document on the matter is privileged, work product, withdrawn or has no
file behind it, there is nothing the analysis may read and it will say so rather
than produce an empty run. See [What the analysis
reads](/analysis/coverage).

chunks.title: How the analysis works
chunks.text:
Every finding carries the same set of decisions: **Approve**, **Reject**, and
under *More* — mark as incorrect, mark as privileged, suppress. A rejected
finding is not raised again.

Only an attorney with a bar number on file can approve AI output. That authority
is derived from the licence recorded on the account, not granted by an
administrator.

chunks.title: The case memo
chunks.text:
The memo is written once the analysis has run, and it is the section most
attorneys open first. It is prose, prepared as of a date, assembled from what
the earlier stages found.

chunks.title: The case memo
chunks.text:
**Executive summary** · **Background**

**Claims** — each with its **elements**, the **supporting facts** on the file
and the **opposing facts** against it.

**Damages** — a narrative, plus a damages model broken down by category with
low, mid and high figures and a total, and a settlement target range.

**Defenses to expect** — each with a danger level, a likelihood, and a
rebuttal.

**Top risks** — each with a severity.

**Strategy** · **Conclusion**

chunks.title: The case memo
chunks.text:
Two sections sit behind the memo.

**Legal research** — authority for the questions the checklist raised, each
carrying a confidence.

**Analogous precedents** — decisions that resemble this matter, and, where the
analysis can say so, what **distinguishes** them.

Each authority is marked by where it came from:

- **Grounded** — from the shared legal-authority corpus the install carries.
- **Live search** — retrieved from CourtListener at run time.

chunks.title: The case memo
chunks.text:
Everything in the memo resolves back to the evidence list, so a supporting fact
carries the document and page it came from. Where the analysis is unsure it says
so with a confidence of low, medium or high rather than omitting the point.

The memo is a draft for an attorney, not a filing, and like everything else the
engine writes it can be approved, rejected or marked incorrect.

chunks.title: Reviewing a run
chunks.text:
**Watch it run** while one is in flight, or **Review the run** afterwards, opens
the run review screen: one version of the analysis, step by step.

chunks.title: Reviewing a run
chunks.text:
The left rail lists the nine steps in order, grouped into five phases — ingest,
frame and retrieve, structure, score and decide, compose and commit. Each step
shows what it is for:

| Step | Its job |
| --- | --- |
| Knowledge base | The same party, spelled four ways, resolved |
| Case summary | State the matter neutrally |
| Research checklist | The questions this matter raises |
| Similar cases | Analogous decisions |
| Legal research | Authority for the questions asked |
| Theory and damages | The theory, the damages, the defences to expect |
| Case assessment | Price the judgement already made |
| Memorandum | The prose an attorney reads first |
| Developments | What changed, and what to do about it |

chunks.title: Reviewing a run
chunks.text:
While a run is going the header shows **Live**, and a ticker across the top
tracks elapsed time, steps finished, current case strength, and steps needing a
look.

Each panel fills in the moment its step writes its row — you do not have to wait
for the run to finish. Scroll away and the screen **detaches** from the live
step rather than dragging you along; scroll back to follow again.

chunks.title: Reviewing a run
chunks.text:
Each step says which it is.

**Required** — if it fails, the run ends there.

**Can be skipped** — if it fails the run carries on without it, and the step
records why. You will see *the run carried on without it; nothing below was
blocked*.

chunks.title: Reviewing a run
chunks.text:
A step marked **carried forward from run 6** was reused: nothing it depends on
had changed. That is what makes an incremental run cheap.

chunks.title: Reviewing a run
chunks.text:
A step with **Not recorded** finished without writing a row — usually because
the step did not exist when that run ran. It is shown anyway so the ladder reads
the same on every run.

chunks.title: Reviewing a run
chunks.text:
The first step is worth opening on its own. It shows the resolved parties with
their aliases (*aka …*), the fact and event counts, what is new since the last
run, the chronology it built, and the **evidence list** every later stage cites
into.

  Stages cite an index into that list, never a quote they composed. The index
  resolves back to the fact, the document and the page — so the worst a model can
  do is cite the wrong one, which points at a real passage that visibly does not
  support the claim.

If the generative merge was unavailable, the step says so: parties were resolved
by normalisation alone, and the knowledge base is usable and may be coarser than
usual.

chunks.title: Reviewing a run
chunks.text:
**Audit history** on the Analysis tab records everything that happened to the
analysis on this matter, including what the engine itself did — actor *Analysis
engine*. **Export CSV** takes the lot.

chunks.title: Case strength
chunks.text:
Every successful run scores the matter out of 100 in ten categories.

| Category | |
| --- | --- |
| **Overall strength** | The headline figure. |
| Liability | Damages |
| Evidence | Witness credibility |
| Defendant exposure | Settlement leverage |
| Trial readiness | Procedural risk |
| Case completion | |

A category the run could not price shows as *not scored*.

chunks.title: Case strength
chunks.text:
A score that changed since the previous version shows its previous value and, on
expansion, **why it moved** — in prose, tied to the developments that caused it.

A score seen for the first time is marked **New**; one that did not move is
marked **No change**.

**Score history** draws the trend across versions for whichever category you
pick, with each point labelled by version and the phase the matter was in.

  A matter getting weaker is shown as plainly as one getting stronger. That is
  the point of keeping every version.

chunks.title: Case strength
chunks.text:
An attorney can override any score with a value and a **required reason**.

The override is what the product then shows, marked **Overridden**, with a note
recording who set it, to what, and what the engine had scored. **Remove
override** hands the category back to the engine.

An override does not silence the engine. Later runs still score the category;
you keep seeing what it thinks alongside what you decided.

chunks.title: Case strength
chunks.text:
**Portfolio strength** splits every analysed matter into four bands — Strong
(80+), Good (60–79), Moderate (40–59), Weak (under 40) — plus the matters not
yet analysed, and gives the firm-wide average.

**Score movement** lists the matters whose overall strength moved most recently,
with the version and when.

Both are scoped to the matters you are on.

chunks.title: Case strength
chunks.section: Where the numbers do not appear
chunks.text:
The run review screen carries no model, token or cost figure. Spend is tracked
for the firm's own books and is not shown on a matter.

chunks.title: Chronology
chunks.text:
The chronology is built from the documents as they land — every dated event the
analysis extracted, merged across documents and put in order. Each row shows how
many documents it came from.

It is also what the case summary, research checklist and theory stages read, so
a wrong row is not cosmetic.

chunks.title: Chronology
chunks.text:
**Correct this event** replaces the extracted wording with yours.

  A row you touch stops being the engine's. Correcting, striking or freezing a
  row takes it off the engine **for good** — no later run rewrites it.

chunks.title: Chronology
chunks.text:
**Date** — as the record puts it. *Early 2020* is a real answer.

**Sorts under** — optional. Where a fuzzy date belongs in the order. Leave it
empty and the row sorts last.

**What happened** — one sentence.

**Who was involved** — names, separated by commas.

chunks.title: Chronology
chunks.text:
**Add event** is for what no document records — the call, the meeting with no
minutes. It is yours from the start; no run will ever touch it. Rows added this
way are marked *Added by hand*.

chunks.title: Chronology
chunks.text:
**Strike from the chronology** removes a row from the timeline without deleting
it. Struck rows are hidden; **Show struck rows** brings them back, and **Put
back** restores one.

A row the documents no longer support is marked *No longer in the documents*
rather than vanishing.

chunks.title: Chronology
chunks.text:
**Freeze this date** pins a row so runs will not rewrite it — useful where the
extractor keeps re-deriving a date you have already settled. **Hand back to the
engine** unfreezes it, and a later run may then rewrite it.

chunks.title: Chronology
chunks.text:
A chronology event happened on a date. A [fact](/analysis/facts) is a
proposition with no date, handed to every stage of every run. Use the one that
fits what you are recording.

chunks.title: The client portal
chunks.section: Client access is a record, not a permission
chunks.text:
The portal reads the list of things **released to it** and nothing else. It
never touches a case, a document list or an analysis run, so there is no flag to
misconfigure.

  An empty released list means an empty portal. That is the whole rule.

A client never appears in a firm-wide user list, a search result or a team
picker. They are counted separately from members for exactly that reason.

chunks.title: The client portal
chunks.text:
**Shared with you** — the documents released on their matter, each with when it
was shared, its page count, and whether it is downloadable or view-only, and
whether it is watermarked.

**Their client channel**, if the lead has opened one. See
[Messaging](/messaging).

Nothing else on the matter is shown, and the portal says so.

chunks.title: The client portal
chunks.text:
**Client tab → Invite the client**.

- Enter their email address.
- Invite a delegate the same way. Each person gets their own account — never a
  shared login.

The invitation **names your firm and never the matter**. Access has no end date;
it ends when the matter closes.

Until somebody accepts, the account shows as *invited … awaiting acceptance*.

  The client portal is a plan capability. On a plan without it, inviting clients
  and releasing documents to them is unavailable — see [Plans and
  limits](/reference/limits).

chunks.title: The client portal
chunks.text:
Inviting the client and releasing to them belong to the **lead attorney** on
that matter. Everyone else sees the ledger and is told that plainly.

chunks.title: The client portal
chunks.text:
The **Client** tab lists everything released, live and revoked: what it was, who
released it, when, during which phase, whether the client was notified, and
whether download and watermarking are on.

Four kinds of thing can appear there: a **document**, a **work artifact**, a
**case update**, and a **client thread**.

chunks.title: Releasing and revoking
chunks.text:
**Release to the client** on a document, from the Documents tab. One document at
a time — there is no bulk release.

The dialog asks for two decisions:

**Allow download.** Off means view-only, which is a real share — the client can
read it, they just cannot take a copy.

**Watermark with their name and the date.** Applied to what they open and to
what they download.

chunks.title: Releasing and revoking
chunks.text:
The document appears in the client's portal. The client is notified and can open
it from that moment. Nothing else on the matter is shared by this.

  This leaves the firm. Revoking later stops future access — it cannot recall
  what has already been read.

chunks.title: Releasing and revoking
chunks.text:
Work product and privileged documents never leave the firm. The release button
refuses, and says so.

A document that is not on this matter cannot be released from it either.

chunks.title: Releasing and revoking
chunks.text:
**Revoke** on the released ledger, on the Client tab. A **reason** is required.

Future access stops immediately, in every session. Anything the client has
already opened or downloaded stays with them.

Revoked entries stay on the ledger, marked **Revoked**, with who revoked them
and when.

chunks.title: Releasing and revoking
chunks.text:
A document that has been released **cannot be withdrawn** from the matter.
Revoke the release first.

Flagging a released document as privileged does not recall it either. Revoke it
separately.

chunks.title: Releasing and revoking
chunks.text:
Advancing a matter's phase re-evaluates what the client is allowed to see and
**releases nothing**. That stays one deliberate click by the lead. Reverting a
phase never un-shares what was already shared.

chunks.title: Type, origin and dates
chunks.text:
The one field on the edit form that the analysis reads back. A document filed as
a deposition is read as one.

Pleading · Email · HR complaint · Performance review · Text message ·
Termination letter · Deposition · Medical record · Expert report · Contract ·
Correspondence · Notes · Other

Untyped documents show as *Not yet typed*.

chunks.title: Type, origin and dates
chunks.text:
Where the document came from, which is a different question from who uploaded
it.

Our client · Opposing party · Third party · Court · Public record · Our work ·
AI generated

Separately, the detail sheet records how it **arrived** — direct upload, email,
an integration, a scan, or AI generated — one row per arrival.

chunks.title: Type, origin and dates
chunks.text:
The date the document is *about*, not the day it was filed.

  A 2023 medical record uploaded this morning is a 2023 document. The list sorts
  on this, the chronology is built from it, and the analysis reasons about it.
  Leave it empty if the document genuinely carries no date.

Where the extractor could not read the date confidently, the document is flagged
**date unclear** and appears under that filter. Editing it and saving records
your answer as the settled one.

chunks.title: Type, origin and dates
chunks.text:
The documents toolbar switches between sorting by **document date** and by
**date filed**, and offers all time, last 30 days, last 90 days and last 12
months windows against whichever you picked.

The side rail filters by type, origin, sensitivity and status — including
*Date unclear* and *Could not be read*.

chunks.title: Type, origin and dates
chunks.text:
**Edit document** from the row menu or the detail sheet. It covers the title,
the document date, the type, the origin and the sensitivity flags.

Titles and dates are facts about one document, so they are not offered in the
bulk editor. Type, origin and sensitivity are.

chunks.title: Duplicates and relations
chunks.text:
Detection compares documents as they arrive and proposes pairs. **Nothing is
merged either way** — a person decides.

  Auto-merging a near-duplicate is how the one copy carrying a handwritten note
  in the margin disappears. Detection proposes; a person confirms.

chunks.title: Duplicates and relations
chunks.text:
A banner on the documents tab counts the pairs awaiting a decision. Opening it
shows each pair with a similarity percentage where one could be computed.

Two answers:

- **Same document** — recorded as the same document.
- **Different** — recorded as two different documents.

Either way the decision is stored with your name and the time, and nothing is
merged or deleted. Answered pairs move to *Already decided*.

chunks.title: Duplicates and relations
chunks.section: The relations a pair can carry
chunks.text:
| Relation | Inverse |
| --- | --- |
| Duplicate of | Duplicate of |
| Near-duplicate of | Near-duplicate of |
| Supersedes | Superseded by |
| Attachment of | Has attachment |
| Exhibit of | Has exhibit |
| Responds to | Answered by |
| Excerpt of | Excerpted in |

They appear under **Related documents** on the detail sheet, from both sides.

chunks.title: Duplicates and relations
chunks.text:
A document can carry several versions — *v2 — current*, *v1 — superseded* — each
recording who filed it. The current version is what the viewer opens and what
the analysis reads.

chunks.title: Duplicates and relations
chunks.text:
These are different things.

An **arrival** is the same bytes reaching the firm again — from another
custodian, or by another route. Filing them records another arrival on the
existing document rather than creating a second one. One stored object, several
rows under *Where it came from*.

A **duplicate** is two documents whose text is similar enough that they may be
the same thing. That is a judgement, and it is yours.

chunks.title: Filing documents
chunks.text:
**Documents → Upload** files one or more documents onto the matter. The files go
straight to storage from your browser; they do not pass through a form post.

Accepted: PDF, image or Word document, up to 200 MB each — subject to your
plan's own single-file limit.

chunks.title: Filing documents
chunks.text:
For each file:

- **Document title** — how it reads in the list. Defaults to the filename.
- **Type** — pleading, email, deposition, medical record, and so on. See
  [Type, origin and dates](/documents/classifying).
- **Origin** — where it came from.
- **Privileged** / **Work product** — tick now, not later.

  A tick here withholds the document from the AI. Privileged and work-product
  documents are never read by the analysis, never quoted in it, and never leave
  the firm. You can change this later from the document itself — but the window
  between filing and reviewing is exactly when it matters.

chunks.title: Filing documents
chunks.section: What happens after you press file
chunks.text:
1. Each file is **fingerprinted** in the browser.
2. It is **uploaded** directly to storage.
3. It is **filed** on the matter and appears in the list immediately.
4. It is **read** in the background. Its text becomes searchable and quotable
   when the read finishes.

Reading runs in the background — keep working. Pages and citations appear as
each document finishes. See [How documents are read](/documents/reading).

chunks.title: Filing documents
chunks.section: If the file is already on the matter
chunks.text:
The fingerprint is checked before anything is filed. If the same bytes are
already on this matter, you are told which document they were filed as, and
filing **records where this copy came from** rather than adding a second
document.

If that same source on that same date is already recorded, there is nothing to
add and the product says so.

This is why the document detail sheet has a **Where it came from** section: one
row per arrival. The same file from two custodians is two rows and one stored
object.

chunks.title: Filing documents
chunks.section: Documents with no file behind them
chunks.text:
A document can exist on a matter with nothing attached — recorded off a
privilege log, or still uploading. It shows as *Recorded, no file attached*.
There is nothing to read, so the analysis skips it and it is counted separately
under coverage.

chunks.title: Filing documents
chunks.text:
| Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Not added — empty or over the size limit | The file is 0 bytes, or larger than your plan allows. |
| The upload didn't finish | A network interruption. Try that file again. |
| That file didn't match its fingerprint and wasn't filed | The bytes changed in transit. Nothing was filed. |
| Document storage isn't configured for this install | An administrator has to set the storage keys. |
| Your plan allows *n* documents per matter | See [Plans and limits](/reference/limits). |

chunks.title: Review, withdraw, bulk changes
chunks.text:
Three states, in the **Review** column:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Unreviewed** | Nobody has signed off on it yet. |
| **Reviewed** | Read and stood behind. Records who read it, and when. |
| **Released** | Released to the client. |

**Mark reviewed** and **Undo review** are on the row menu. Marking a document
reviewed is not sharing it — that is a separate decision, made by the lead
attorney from the Documents tab.

chunks.title: Review, withdraw, bulk changes
chunks.text:
**Withdraw from the matter** takes a document off the matter. It stops appearing
in the document list and the analysis no longer opens it.

  Nothing is destroyed. The document and its original file are kept in full, and
  this can be undone with **Restore**. The same file may also be filed on
  another matter — withdrawing it here does not touch that one.

A **reason** is required. It is kept with the document and written to the audit
log, because whoever asks about this later is asking exactly that.

Two things block a withdrawal:

- **The document has been released to the client.** Revoke that release first.
- **Somebody changed the document while your screen was open.** Reload and try
  again.

chunks.title: Review, withdraw, bulk changes
chunks.text:
Select documents with the row checkboxes. The bulk bar offers:

**Reclassify** — type, origin and each sensitivity flag, every control
three-way: *leave*, *set*, *clear*. Anything left alone stays as it is. Titles
and dates are not offered, because they are facts about one document. Each
change is written to the audit log against its own document.

**Read again** — queues the whole selection for reading.

**Withdraw** — one typed reason covers the set, and is kept with every document
in it.

**Release stays one document at a time.** There is no bulk release.

chunks.title: Review, withdraw, bulk changes
chunks.text:
Opening a document's details shows everything filed behind it:

- Document date, date filed, how it arrived, page count, size, fingerprint.
- Review state, with what that state currently permits.
- Versions, with who filed each.
- Where it came from — one row per arrival.
- Related documents.
- **Access history**, append-only. Each line records the role its actor held at
  the time, not the role they hold now.

The audit lines you will see: opened it, changed its details, withdrew it, put
it back, released it to the client, asked for it to be read again, answered a
duplicate match, recorded another arrival, marked it reviewed, took the review
back.

chunks.title: How documents are read
chunks.text:
Every file filed on a matter is read in the background. Reading extracts the
text **with the page it came from**, which is what lets a finding in the
analysis point at a page rather than at a document.

Until a document has been read it has no pages, and nothing in it can be cited.

chunks.title: How documents are read
chunks.text:
| State | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Queued** | Filed and waiting its turn. | Nothing. Pages appear once it has been read. |
| **Reading** | Being read now. | Nothing. Pages and citations follow when it finishes. |
| **Stalled** | Queued, and it has not moved since. | Nothing will pick it up on its own. Ask for it to be read again. |
| **Unreadable** | Reading did not finish. No pages, nothing citable. | Ask for it to be read again. If it keeps failing, the file is likely damaged or is a scan the parser cannot handle. |
| **Not read** | Nothing has read the file yet, so its length is unknown. | |
| **No file** | Recorded on the matter with nothing behind it. | Nothing to read. Upload the file if you have it. |

The number of documents currently being read is shown above the list.

chunks.title: How documents are read
chunks.text:
**Read again** from the document's row menu, from its detail sheet, or on a
selection of documents at once from the bulk bar.

Bytes already read under the current settings are re-used rather than
re-parsed, so a re-read of a healthy document is cheap. It is worth doing when a
document is stalled or unreadable, or after the file itself was replaced.

chunks.title: How documents are read
chunks.text:
Reading does not classify the document, decide its date, or judge it. It
produces text and page boundaries. Everything else — the type, the origin, the
document date, the sensitivity flags — is yours, and the analysis reads those
back. A document filed as a deposition is read as one.

  Where a browser cannot draw the file type at all, the viewer falls back to
  showing what the parser read out of it. If it has not been read yet, there is
  nothing to show — which is what *Nothing to show yet* in the viewer means.

chunks.title: How documents are read
chunks.text:
As documents are read, their text is compared against what is already on the
matter, and near-duplicates are proposed for a decision. Nothing is merged
either way. See [Duplicates and relations](/documents/duplicates).

chunks.title: Privilege and sensitivity
chunks.text:
Withheld from production **and from AI retrieval**. Its text is never retrieved,
never quoted in an analysis, and never produced.

Setting the flag asks for a **basis for the privilege claim** — for example,
*attorney-client, advice sought from counsel on the termination*. That text is
kept with the document.

chunks.title: Privilege and sensitivity
Privilege and sensitivity
chunks.text:
Editing a document to *add* a flag tells you plainly: *this will be withheld
from the AI*. Its text stops being retrievable and stops reaching anyone outside
the firm.

Removing a flag says the opposite: *this will be readable by the AI*. Nothing
changes until you save; saving is what makes it eligible.

  A copy already released to the client cannot be recalled by flagging the
  document. Revoke that release separately — and even revoking cannot recall
  what has already been read.

chunks.title: Privilege and sensitivity
chunks.text:
- **Flags** column and the sensitivity filters on the document list.
- **Handle with care** on the document detail sheet, spelling out what the flag
  is currently doing.
- **Withheld** in the analysis [coverage panel](/analysis/coverage), with the
  reason.
- The bulk editor, where each flag is a three-way control: leave, set, or clear.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.text:
A single compromised password against a privileged document store is the whole
  risk in one event. That is why this is a firm rule and not a per-person
  preference.

Turning it on stops anyone not yet enrolled **on their next request** — not at
their next sign-in — until they have set it up. The screen tells you how many
members that is before you save.

**Who is covered** counts enrolled members against active members and names the
ones without a second factor.

Members enrol from [Your account](/account). If somebody genuinely cannot set it
up, an administrator can lift the requirement here.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.text:
Some acts cannot be undone. Asking for the password again at the moment of the
act costs three seconds and turns the most dangerous clicks in the product into
deliberate ones.

Three acts can be covered:

| Act | Why it is on the list |
| --- | --- |
| **Changing a colleague's role** | A role is the ceiling on every matter they are assigned to. |
| **Deactivating a member** | Ends their access to the firm. Reversible, but not by them. |
| **Weakening this policy** | Turning the two-factor requirement off, or removing an act from this list. |

Strengthening the policy never asks.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.text:
When one fires you get **Confirm your password** — your current password, and
nothing else. *It takes three seconds and it is what stops an unattended screen
from becoming an incident.*

A wrong password fails the act; nothing is half-applied.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.text:
| Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Your role cannot change the firm's authentication policy | Owner or administrator only. |
| Confirm your password to make this change | Step-up is required for this act. |
| That password is not right | The act was not performed. |

chunks.title: Billing and plans
chunks.text:
**Firm Settings → Billing** shows the current plan, its status, usage against
each meter, and every tier including the one you are on.

Firm owners and the billing role can manage it.

chunks.title: Billing and plans
chunks.text:
| Status | |
| --- | --- |
| **Trial** | A new firm's first 30 days. |
| **Active** | |
| **Payment failed** | We could not take payment. Full access continues while we retry — update the card. |
| **Paused** | |
| **Cancelled** | The plan ends at the close of the current period. |

chunks.title: Billing and plans
chunks.text:
Active matters · People · Documents stored · Analyses this period.

Active matters counts both **active** and **on hold**. Drafts are free. Seats
count members **and pending invitations** — an invitation nobody has accepted
still holds a seat.

chunks.title: Billing and plans
chunks.text:
The product refuses the new thing and tells you which limit and by how much. It
never deletes, hides or degrades what is already there.

  **New work is paused** — the trial ended, or the subscription is not active.
  Every matter, document and analysis stays readable and downloadable. Choose a
  plan to add new work again.

Typical refusals:

- Your plan covers *n* active matters and your firm has *m*.
- Every seat on your plan is taken, counting invitations nobody has accepted yet.
- Your plan allows *n* documents per matter and this one already has *m*.
- That file is over the single-file limit on your plan.
- Your firm has used *x* of its *y* of document storage.
- Your plan includes *n* analyses per billing period and your firm has used *m*.
- The client portal / messaging is not included in your firm's plan.

chunks.title: Billing and plans
chunks.text:
Pick a tier to compare it — nothing is charged until you continue.

- Moving onto a paid plan changes it as soon as the card is saved. **A trial
  still runs to its end date before anything is charged.**
- Moving between paid plans is handled by Stripe, including the proration and
  the invoice for the difference.
- **Enterprise** is negotiated. Contact sales.
- The trial is only available when a firm first signs up.

**Manage billing** opens Stripe for plan changes, invoices, receipts and
cancellation.

chunks.title: Billing and plans
chunks.text:
See [Plans and limits](/reference/limits) for the full table.

If the screen says *billing is not configured on this deployment*, this install
has no payment provider wired up. Contact your account team.

chunks.title: The firm
chunks.text:
**Firm Settings** carries the rules that apply to every matter. Your own
credentials and preferences live on [Your account](/account).

Firm owners and firm administrators can open it. Everyone else is told the
screen exists and cannot open it: *your role does not include changing firm-wide
rules or the roster*.

chunks.title: The firm
chunks.text:
**Firm name** — how the firm reads everywhere.

**Main jurisdiction**

**Matter types** — every kind of matter the firm takes. These lead the list on a
new case, above every other type. At least one must stay selected.

**Retention (years)** — how long after closing a matter stays before it becomes
eligible for deletion. The clock starts at close.

  A legal hold outranks retention. A held matter is never deleted, whatever this
  setting says.

**Record** — the workspace slug and the date the firm was opened. Read-only.

chunks.title: The firm
chunks.text:
**Open a new firm** in the workspace switcher creates a separate firm with its
own cases, members and retention. Nothing is shared with the firms you are
already in, and you become its owner.

You will not be able to approve AI output or release anything until a bar number
is recorded on your account.

chunks.title: The firm
chunks.text:
| Tab | |
| --- | --- |
| **Firm** | This page. |
| **People** | Members, invitations, external access, client accounts, walls, recent access changes. |
| **Roles & access** | What each role can do, and the four qualifiers on top of it. |
| **Authentication** | Two-factor policy and step-up re-authentication. |
| **Billing** | Plan, usage and invoices. |

chunks.title: People and invitations
chunks.text:
The roster shows every member with their role, how many matters they are on,
how many they lead, whether they can approve AI output, their state, and their
last session.

A role here is the **ceiling**. None of it reaches a matter until they are
assigned to one.

chunks.title: People and invitations
chunks.text:
**Invite** sends a link to a work email. It expires in **seven days**, and
joining through it verifies the address.

The roles you can hand out from this screen: firm admin, attorney, paralegal,
staff, billing.

  Clients and outside experts are **not** invited here. A client belongs to a
  matter; an outsider gets a scoped grant with an expiry. Both are created
  through the case.

**Waiting on an answer** lists open invitations with who sent each and when it
expires. **Cancel** withdraws one.

chunks.title: People and invitations
chunks.text:
**Manage member → Role**. Nobody may change their own role: being able to raise
your own would make every other permission in the product decorative.

Your firm may require your password again before this takes effect — see
[Authentication](/firm/authentication).

chunks.title: People and invitations
chunks.text:
**Deactivate** ends their access to the firm. It is reversible with **Restore
access**, though not by them.

Two refusals you may hit:

- **They still lead at least one matter.** Transfer the lead first. A case
  cannot be left without a lead attorney, even for an afternoon.
- **A firm cannot be left without an owner.**

  A deactivated member is never deleted. Their name stays on every approval,
  release and audit line they created, with the role they held at the time.

chunks.title: People and invitations
chunks.section: The other panels on this tab
chunks.text:
**External access, across every matter** — every outstanding grant, the number
of documents it reaches, and which are expiring. Created from the matter, never
from here.

**Client accounts** — portal-only accounts, counted separately from members
because a client reads a released list and never the case record.

**Ethical walls** — every wall in place, as *person — matter*, with who set it
and when. Set from the matter it applies to. See [Ethical walls](/team/walls).

**Recent access changes** — invitations, case grants, walls and deactivations,
sorted by time.

  Recent access changes is **not the audit log**. It is the four
  access-affecting writes this screen records, and nothing else.

chunks.title: CaseWize Help
chunks.text:
CaseWize is case management with a case-intelligence engine underneath it. A
firm opens a matter, files what it has, and the documents become searchable text
with the page they came from still attached. An analysis runs on top of that and
produces findings an attorney can act on — a chronology, the parties, the
contradictions, the gaps, what to do next — while tasks, messaging and the
client portal keep the work and the client in the same place.

This help centre describes the product as it ships. What you actually see is
narrowed by two things: your firm role, and whether you are on the matter at
all.

chunks.title: CaseWize Help
chunks.text:
**Ask AI** in the top bar answers questions from these pages and links to the
ones it used. It knows the product; it cannot see your firm, your matters or
your documents.

chunks.title: CaseWize Help
chunks.section: Four things worth knowing before anything else
chunks.text:
**A role is a ceiling, not an assignment.** Being an attorney says what you may
do on a matter you are on. It does not put you on one. A firm owner who has not
been added to a matter cannot open it.

**Privilege and work product are excluded by the system, not by a setting.** A
document flagged either way is never read by the analysis, never quoted in it,
and never leaves the firm. No role, grant or plan turns that back on.

**Analysis is versioned, never overwritten.** Every run is a numbered version.
Scores, developments and findings hang off it, so you can see what a matter
looked like three runs ago and what moved since.

**The client sees a list, not the case.** The portal reads what has been
released to it and nothing else. There is no permission to misconfigure because
there is no connection to the case record.

chunks.title: Inside the case file
chunks.text:
**Cases** shows the matters you are on — and only those. A matter you are
screened off is absent from the table, the counts and the search alike, rather
than hidden inside them.

Columns: case, phase, status, statute deadline, parties, lead, last activity,
and what is waiting on you. Filter by phase across the top. A **Hold** badge
means a legal hold is set and nothing on that matter deletes while it stands.

Above the table, **Needs attention** collects two things:

- a statute deadline inside 30 days (or already passed),
- no activity on the file for 30 days.

chunks.title: Inside the case file
chunks.section: Status and phase at a glance
chunks.text:
**Status** is the matter's lifecycle: draft, active, on hold, closed, archived.

**Phase** is where the litigation stands: investigation, discovery, expert
reports, mediation, trial.

Both are explained on [Phase, status and holds](/matters/lifecycle).

chunks.title: Inside the case file
chunks.text:
The first thing you see when you open a matter.

**Case strength** — the overall score from the most recent analysis, its
version, and whether it moved. If the matter has never been analysed, this
panel tells you so and offers to start one.

**Open alerts** — what the analysis has raised and nobody has acknowledged.

**Next actions** — recommended actions, most urgent first.

**Material developments** — what the analysis judged material since last time.

**On this matter** — open tasks with overdue and due-this-week counts, the
document count, and the number of chronology events.

Down the side: the statute deadline with days remaining, the lead attorney, the
team size including external grants, the party count, and the conflict-check
result.

chunks.title: Inside the case file
chunks.text:
The overview also carries the controls for advancing the phase, closing the
matter, and setting or lifting a legal hold. See
[Phase, status and holds](/matters/lifecycle).

chunks.title: Inside the case file
chunks.text:
**"You can see this matter exists. You cannot open the file."** You have a
metadata-only view — the firm-admin position. You can manage the roster; you
cannot read the matter.

**"You administer this matter. You cannot read it."** The same thing, said on
the matter itself. There is no setting that changes it.

**"That matter is not available to you."** You are not on it, and for you it
does not exist.

  Every rule on these pages is enforced when a request is resolved, not when a
  screen is drawn. Hiding a button is not access control, and a disabled input
  is not either — a change you are not allowed to make simply will not save.

chunks.title: Opening a matter
chunks.text:
**New case** starts a four-step intake. It is saved as a draft the moment you
continue past step 1, and only you can see your own drafts — they appear on the
case list under *Your unfinished intakes*. A draft is a lead, not a case.

Only a licensed attorney or the firm owner can take a matter on.

chunks.title: Opening a matter
chunks.text:
Nothing here is checked yet.

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| **Internal number** | Yours, assigned now. Unique within the firm — a second matter cannot take the same string. |
| **Court number** | Stays empty until a suit is filed. A case is real before a court knows about it. |
| **Case title** | How the matter reads everywhere in the product. |
| **Matter type** | The types your firm takes are listed first; every other type is below them. |
| **Jurisdiction** | |
| **Court** | |
| **Phase** | Where the matter actually stands today, not where it starts on paper. |

chunks.title: Opening a matter
chunks.text:
Covered in full on [Parties and conflicts](/matters/parties). In short: the
conflict check has nothing to search until at least the client is attached, and
it re-runs every time a party is added or removed.

chunks.title: Opening a matter
chunks.text:
The two fields the database will not let an active matter go without.

**Statute deadline** — the final date by which the firm must file. No override,
no TBD. A missed statute of limitations kills the claim permanently.

**Lead attorney** — only members holding a bar number appear in this list. The
same licence is what grants the right to approve an AI run later.

  Not in the list yourself? If your bar number is not on file, record it and the
  state that issued it on **Your account** and you will be taken straight back
  to this step. If you are not an attorney or firm owner, you cannot lead a
  matter at all — ask an attorney to take it on.

chunks.title: Opening a matter
chunks.text:
The review step shows everything you entered, who will be able to open the
matter, the retention it inherits from the firm profile, and exactly what
pressing **Activate** writes:

chunks.title: Opening a matter
chunks.text:
Two, to begin with — you and the lead. Every later grant, wall or role change
recomputes them rather than being read on the fly at request time.

chunks.title: Opening a matter
chunks.text:
A draft cannot go active until all three are satisfied. The review step tracks
them as *Still outstanding*.

1. **A statute deadline.**
2. **A lead attorney.**
3. **A cleared conflict check** — run, and either clear or cleared in writing by
   an attorney.

The first two are constraints on the row itself: an active matter without them
simply fails to save, whatever the screen does. The third is the product's own —
a firm can be made to record a decision, and cannot be made to make a good one.

chunks.title: Opening a matter
chunks.section: Who can open it once it is live
chunks.text:
**You** — as creator: write, and manage the team.

**The lead** — approve, release, and manage the team.

**Everyone else at the firm** — no access row, so no trace. Not in counts, not
in search.

  Being firm owner is not access to a matter. It is a ceiling on what you could
  do once somebody puts you on one.

chunks.title: Phase, status and holds
chunks.text:
Where the litigation actually stands: **Investigation → Discovery → Expert
reports → Mediation → Trial**. Advance or revert it from the overview tab.

Advancing re-evaluates what the client is allowed to see and **releases
nothing** — that stays one deliberate click by the lead attorney. Reverting
never un-shares what was already shared.

A phase change is one of the triggers that starts a fresh analysis run.

  The analysis has a phase vocabulary of its own, finer than this one — intake,
  pre-filing, pleadings, written discovery, depositions, expert discovery,
  mediation, summary judgment, pretrial, trial preparation. It is what the
  engine judges the matter to be in, and it appears on each run.

chunks.title: Phase, status and holds
chunks.text:
| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Draft** | An unfinished intake. Only its creator sees it. |
| **Active** | Live. |
| **On hold** | Paused, and still counted against your plan's active-matter limit. |
| **Closed** | Frozen for every role. |
| **Archived** | Past its retention window. |

chunks.title: Phase, status and holds
chunks.text:
**Close the matter** on the overview tab. An **outcome** is required — settled,
dismissed, verdict, and so on.

Closing freezes writes for every role and starts the retention clock. Nothing on
a closed matter is editable by anybody: its tasks go read-only, its message
composer disappears while the history stays, and its settings stop saving.

Only the firm owner can reopen it.

chunks.title: Phase, status and holds
chunks.text:
Retention comes from the firm profile — a number of years after closing, set in
**Firm Settings → Firm**. The clock starts at close, not at open.

A legal hold outranks it: a held matter is never deleted, whatever the retention
setting says.

chunks.title: Phase, status and holds
chunks.text:
A legal hold freezes deletion of the matter and everything under it — documents,
versions, and the audit trail. Setting one requires a typed reason, kept
permanently.

- An attorney or the firm owner can **set** a hold.
- Only the firm owner can **lift** one, with a reason kept forever.
- The hold stops deletion, not editing. Fields still save; nothing is destroyed
  while it is on.

  Destroying material the firm is required to keep can be treated as destroying
  evidence. That is why lifting a hold sits with one person and is recorded.

chunks.title: Parties and conflicts
chunks.section: A party exists once at the firm
chunks.text:
A party is an entity the firm knows — a person or a company — attached to a
matter **in a role**. The same company can be the opposing party on one matter
and a witness on another without becoming two records, and its history follows
it.

When you type a name the firm already knows, you are offered the option to
**link** rather than create. Linking reuses that party's history everywhere it
appears. Nothing is merged for you: if they are genuinely different entities,
keep them separate.

chunks.title: Parties and conflicts
chunks.section: The roles a party can hold
chunks.text:
Client · Plaintiff · Defendant · Opposing party · Opposing counsel · Counsel ·
Insurer · Employer · Witness · Expert · Judge · Court · Other

chunks.title: Parties and conflicts
chunks.text:
Every add and every removal re-runs the check **against every party on every
matter the firm has ever opened**, as the system rather than as you.

That distinction matters: it sees matters you cannot open. A match on a walled
or unassigned matter is reported as a match, but the matter is not named and
nobody on it is named. A match you cannot see is still a match.

Three results:

| Result | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Clear** | Nothing matched. |
| **Possible** | Something matched and needs a judgement. |
| **Conflict** | A direct match. |

For each match you are told the role the party held and whether the other matter
is live or closed — and, where you have access to it, which matter.

chunks.title: Parties and conflicts
chunks.text:
An attorney has to clear it in writing before the matter can leave draft. The
reason field is required, and the clearance is recorded with your name and the
time. It is kept permanently, whether the check came back clear or not.

  The check is recorded, not decided. The product can make a firm write down why
  it is proceeding; it cannot make that a good reason.

chunks.title: Parties and conflicts
chunks.text:
Once documents have been read, the analysis proposes parties it found in them —
under **Found in the documents** on the Parties tab. Each proposal tells you
whether the firm already knows that name, how many other matters it appears on,
and how many documents on this matter mention it.

Nothing joins the matter until you accept it. Accepting adds the party to the
firm's records **and re-runs the conflict check**.

Where the documents do not make clear which side you act for, the proposal says
so and you switch the role yourself.

chunks.title: Parties and conflicts
chunks.text:
A party filed under more than one spelling is shown with *also filed as* on the
intake screen, and the analysis's knowledge-base stage resolves the same party
spelled several ways into one entry before any other stage reads it.

chunks.title: Case settings
chunks.text:
The **Settings** tab edits the matter itself — the same fields the intake
collected, after it went live. Everything saves as one change, written against
the matter.

chunks.title: Case settings
chunks.text:
**Internal number** — unique within the firm. Changing it renames the file
everywhere it appears.

**Court number** — filled in the day the suit is filed.

**Case title**

chunks.title: Case settings
chunks.section: What the matter cannot go without
chunks.text:
**Statute deadline** and **lead attorney**, both required. The row fails to save
without them, whatever the screen does.

The lead field is read-only here for most people: handing a matter over is done
from the **Team** tab, by the outgoing lead or the firm owner, and it carries
its own decision about whether the outgoing lead stays on the matter.

chunks.title: Case settings
chunks.text:
| State | What you see |
| --- | --- |
| **Draft** | A draft is edited in the intake wizard, which owns the conflict check and the blockers. Finish it there. |
| **Closed** | Nothing on a closed matter is editable by any role. Reopening is the firm owner's. |
| **Read-only for you** | You can open the file but not change it. Nothing is hidden — it simply will not save. |
| **Walled / metadata-only** | You administer this matter and cannot read it. |

  A legal hold does not close the settings tab. The hold stops deletion, not
  editing.

chunks.title: Messaging
chunks.text:
Three kinds of conversation:

- **Case team** — a thread on a matter, among the people on it.
- **Client channel** — the one thread a matter can have with its client.
- **Direct message** — person to person at the firm.

**Inbox** collects all of them. A matter's **Messages** tab shows only its own.

chunks.title: Messaging
chunks.text:
**New thread** on a matter asks for a subject, an audience and a first message.

**Who's in it** — you are added automatically; uncheck anyone it is not for.
Only people already on the matter can be added.

chunks.title: Messaging
chunks.text:
A client channel is **created shut**. The client cannot see it until the **lead
attorney** opens it with **Open to client**.

Until then it shows *not yet open to the client*, and the dashboard marks it
*Unreleased*.

A matter has at most one client channel. If one already exists, you are pointed
at it.

The client's own seats are added automatically; everyone else is your choice.
The client's seat is opened and closed by release, not from the thread roster.

  Messaging is a plan capability. On a plan without it, case threads and direct
  messages are unavailable — see [Plans and limits](/reference/limits).

chunks.title: Messaging
chunks.text:
Dropping a file into the composer does not attach it to the thread.

  Files live on the matter, not in a thread. File it under **Documents**, then
  **cite** it here.

**Cite** searches the matter's documents and tasks and links one into the
message. A citation the reader is not allowed to see shows as *Withheld* rather
than leaking its title.

chunks.title: Messaging
chunks.text:
Type `@` to name someone on the thread. They get a notification — *… named you
in a conversation*. Only people on the thread match.

chunks.title: Messaging
chunks.text:
**In this thread** lists who is in it. Add anyone on the matter; remove anyone
who should not be. Additions and removals are written into the thread itself as
system lines.

chunks.title: Notifications
chunks.text:
**Notifications** lists what you have been told, newest first. The bell in the
top bar carries the unread count and **Mark all read** clears it.

chunks.title: Notifications
chunks.text:
| Kind | Raised when |
| --- | --- |
| **Mentions** | Somebody names you in a thread. |
| **Task assignments** | A task is put in your name. |
| **Task due dates** | Once, on the morning a task of yours comes due. |

Analysis alerts are configured **per matter**, not here — see [Developments and
alerts](/analysis/developments#choosing-what-you-are-told-about).

chunks.title: Notifications
chunks.text:
Notices reach you **in the app either way**. The email settings on [Your
account](/account) decide which of them also reach your inbox, at that firm.

Each firm you belong to has its own setting.

chunks.title: Notifications
chunks.text:
*On a matter you can no longer open.* A notice raised before your access
  changed stays in your list, with its subject removed. The notice is not
  deleted — that would rewrite history — and its contents are not shown.

chunks.title: Notifications
chunks.text:
Alert email carries the case number and the kind of development, **never the
facts**. Nothing substantive about a matter is sent to an inbox.

chunks.title: Glossary
chunks.text:
**Alert** — a development the analysis judged urgent enough to surface on its
own. New, acknowledged, dismissed or resolved.

**Arrival** — a record that the same file reached the firm again, from another
custodian or by another route. Several arrivals, one stored object.

**Case access** — the computed answer to whether you can open a matter, and what
you can do on it. Recomputed whenever a grant, wall or role changes.

**Case file** — everything filed on a matter.

**Client account** — a portal-only account belonging to a matter. Reads what has
been released and never the case record.

**Coverage** — what an analysis run was allowed to read, and what was withheld
from it and why.

**Development** — something the analysis judged material since the last run.

**Disclosure / release** — the record that a specific document was made
available to the client. The portal reads these rows and nothing else.

**Draft** — an unfinished intake. Visible only to its creator. A lead, not a
case.

**Ethical wall** — a deny that removes a matter from one person entirely. Beats
every role, including the firm owner's.

**Evidence gap** — something the analysis expected on the file and could not
find, with a suggested way to get it.

**Evidence list** — the indexed set of facts a run's stages cite into. A citation
resolves back to the fact, the document and the page.

chunks.title: Glossary
chunks.text:
**External grant** — access for someone outside the firm to **named documents on
one matter**, with a mandatory expiry.

**Fact** — a proposition an attorney recorded. Handed to every later run; a
locked one is treated as settled.

**Firm role** — the ceiling on what you are capable of. Eight of them.

**Incremental run** — a run that reuses the stages nothing changed under.

**Lead attorney** — exactly one per matter. The only person who may release
anything to the client.

**Legal hold** — a freeze on deletion of a matter and everything under it. Set by
an attorney or the owner; lifted only by the owner.

**Materiality** — how much a development matters: critical, high, moderate, low,
informational.

**Matter** — a case. The unit of work.

**Metadata-only access** — you can see that a matter exists and manage its
roster; you cannot read the file. The firm-administrator position.

**Party** — an entity the firm knows, attached to matters in roles. It exists
once and carries its history across matters.

**Phase** — where the litigation stands. Investigation, discovery, expert
reports, mediation, trial.

**Retention** — how long after closing a matter is kept. Outranked by a legal
hold.

**Run** — one execution of the analysis. Produces a numbered version.

**Stage** — one step of a run. Nine of them, each writing its own row.

chunks.title: Glossary
chunks.text:
**Step-up** — being asked for your password again at the moment of an
irreversible act.

**Strength** — the score out of 100 the analysis puts on a matter, overall and in
nine other categories.

**Version** — a numbered analysis result. Never overwritten.

**Withdrawn** — taken off a matter without being destroyed. Restorable.

**Work product** — the firm's own analysis. Never retrieved by the AI, never
released.

chunks.title: Plans and limits
chunks.text:
| | Free trial | Professional | Firm | Enterprise |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Active matters | 1 | 25 | 100 | Negotiated |
| People (seats) | 5 | 5 | 20 | Negotiated |
| Documents per matter | 5 | Unlimited | Unlimited | Negotiated |
| Largest single file | 10 MB | 250 MB | 500 MB | Negotiated |
| Document storage | 100 MB | 250 GB | 1 TB | Negotiated |
| Analyses per period | 2 | 500 | 2,500 | Negotiated |
| Tasks per matter | 5 | Unlimited | Unlimited | Negotiated |
| Client portal | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Messaging | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

The **free trial** runs for 30 days. It exists to prove the product on a single
matter, not to run a practice, which is why every cap is deliberately small.

**Enterprise** is negotiated per firm, with onboarding, review sessions and a
named point of contact.

chunks.title: Plans and limits
chunks.text:
**Active matters** — counted across *active* and *on hold*. Drafts are free, and
closed matters do not count.

**Seats** — firm members **plus pending invitations**. An invitation nobody has
accepted still holds a seat. Clients and externals are not seats.

**Analyses per period** — runs that actually called a model, within the current
billing period. A run that carried everything forward does not count.

**Document storage** — across the whole firm.

chunks.title: Plans and limits
chunks.text:
The refusal is specific: which limit, what your plan covers, and what your firm
has used. Nothing already in the product is deleted, hidden or degraded.

chunks.title: Plans and limits
chunks.text:
When a trial ends or a subscription stops, the firm goes **plan-locked**:

  Every matter, document and analysis stays readable and downloadable. New work
  is paused until a plan is chosen.

chunks.title: Plans and limits
chunks.text:
A failed payment does **not** pause anything while it is retried. Full access
continues; update the card to avoid interruption.

chunks.title: Plans and limits
chunks.text:
You will meet these as refusals in ordinary flows: opening a matter (active
matters), inviting a colleague (seats), uploading (documents per matter, file
size, storage), running an analysis (analyses per period), and adding a task
(tasks per matter).

chunks.title: What a message means
chunks.text:
| Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| You can see this matter exists. You cannot open the file. | Metadata-only access — the firm-administrator position. Not a mistake, and no setting changes it. |
| You administer this matter. You cannot read it. | The same thing, said on the matter. |
| That matter is not available to you. | You are not on it. |
| Your role does not allow that. | Your firm role's ceiling, not your assignment. |
| Your seat at this firm could not be confirmed. Sign in again. | Your membership changed mid-session. |
| Firm Settings is administered by the firm. | Owner or administrator only. |

chunks.title: What a message means
chunks.text:
| Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Another matter at the firm already uses that file number. | Internal numbers are unique within the firm. |
| The conflict check has to come back clear, or be cleared in writing, first. | An attorney must clear it with a reason. |
| A lead attorney has to hold a bar number. | Record it on Your account. |
| That matter is no longer a draft. | Somebody activated it while your screen was open. |

chunks.title: What a message means
chunks.text:
| Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| A matter cannot be left without a lead. Transfer it first. | Applies to removing a lead and to deactivating a member who leads one. |
| The new lead has to be on the matter first. | Add them to the roster, then transfer. |
| They still lead at least one matter. | Deactivation refused for the same reason. |

chunks.title: What a message means
chunks.text:
| Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| This document has been released to the client. Revoke that release before withdrawing it. | Release must be revoked first. |
| Somebody changed this document while your screen was open. | Reload and try again. |
| This document has no file attached, so there is nothing to read. | Recorded without a file. |
| Work product and privileged documents cannot be released. | A hardcoded exclusion, not a permission. |
| One of those documents is not on this matter, or is work product or privileged. | Applies to external grants. |
| That file didn't match its fingerprint and wasn't filed. | The bytes changed in transit. Nothing was filed. |
| Document storage isn't configured for this install. | An administrator has to set the storage keys. |

chunks.title: What a message means
chunks.text:
| Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| There is nothing on this matter the analysis may read. | Everything present is privileged, work product, withdrawn, or has no file. |
| Some stages failed. | A skippable stage did not finish. The run carried on, and the step records why. |
| No change | The run finished and found nothing that moved the matter. |
| Carried forward | The stage was reused because nothing it depends on changed. |

chunks.title: What a message means
chunks.text:
| Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| This matter is closed. Reopen it before making changes. | Only the firm owner can reopen. |
| A legal hold is set. Nothing on this matter can be deleted. | The hold stops deletion, not editing. |

chunks.title: What a message means
chunks.text:
| Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Your plan does not stretch this far. | A limit was reached. See [Plans and limits](/reference/limits). |
| New work is paused on this plan. | Trial over or subscription inactive. Everything stays readable. |
| Your plan does not include this feature. | A capability, not a limit — the client portal or messaging. |
| Every seat on your plan is taken. | Counting invitations nobody has accepted yet. |

chunks.title: What a message means
chunks.text:
| Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Set up two-factor authentication to continue. | Your firm requires it, and it applies now rather than at your next sign-in. |
| Confirm your password to make this change. | Step-up re-authentication for an irreversible act. |
| That code was not accepted. | Usually a phone clock that has drifted. |
| Too many failed codes. | The account is locked for a short period. |

chunks.title: What a message means
chunks.text:
| Message | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| That would make two tasks depend on each other. | Dependency cycles are refused. |
| Something it's waiting on is still open. | A prerequisite has to close first. |
| The matter is closed, so its tasks are read-only. | |

chunks.title: Your first matter
chunks.text:
If you are an attorney, open **Your account** and record your state bar number
and the state that issued it. Approval authority is derived from that licence,
not granted by a checkbox: without it you cannot be made lead on a matter and
cannot approve AI output.

chunks.title: Your first matter
chunks.text:
**New case** starts a four-step intake. Step 1 is the matter itself — internal
number, case title, matter type, jurisdiction, court, phase. Nothing is checked
yet, and the moment you continue it is saved as a draft only you can see.

chunks.title: Your first matter
chunks.text:
Step 2. Add the client first, then anyone else — opposing party, opposing
counsel, insurer, witnesses. Each one runs a conflict check against every party
on every matter the firm has ever opened, as the system rather than as you, so
it sees matters you cannot.

If something matches, an attorney has to clear it in writing with a reason
before the matter can leave draft.

chunks.title: Your first matter
chunks.section: Set the deadline and the lead
chunks.text:
Step 3, and the two fields a live matter cannot exist without: the statute
deadline, and a lead attorney. Only members with a bar number on file appear in
the lead list.

chunks.title: Your first matter
chunks.text:
Step 4 shows exactly what activating writes: the matter goes live with your id
on it permanently as creator, the parties and their roles are kept, the conflict
result and your reason are kept whether it came back clear or not, and the
access rows are computed.

Two people can open it at this point — you, and the lead. Nobody else at the
firm has an access row, so for them the matter does not exist.

chunks.title: Your first matter
chunks.text:
