Open **Documents → Upload**. Files go straight to storage from your browser.
Mark anything privileged or work product *now*, on the upload form, rather than
after review — that tick is what keeps it out of the analysis.

Each document is read in the background. It appears in the list immediately; its
text becomes searchable and quotable when the read finishes.

chunks.title: Your first matter
chunks.text:
The first analysis starts as soon as a document has been read, or you can start
one by hand from the **Analysis** tab. Watch it run if you want to see the
stages land one by one.

When it finishes you have a case summary, a set of scores with an overall
strength, evidence gaps, contradictions, recommended actions and a memo — every
finding citing the document and page it came from.

chunks.title: Your first matter
chunks.text:
Turn a recommended action into a task. Answer the duplicate matches waiting on a
decision. Correct any chronology row the extractor got wrong. Record facts the
documents do not contain. Each of those feeds the next run.

chunks.title: Your first matter
chunks.text:
Invite the client from the **Client** tab, then release a document from
**Documents**. Only the lead attorney can release, one document at a time, and
the client sees that document and nothing else on the matter.

  Releasing is the one action in the product that reaches outside the firm.
  Revoking later stops future access; it cannot recall what has already been
  read.

chunks.title: Your first matter
chunks.section: What happens on its own after that
chunks.text:
- A new document is read, and an analysis re-runs against the changed file.
- Developments appear under **What changed**, with the score movement they caused.
- Alerts are raised for the things that need attention, at the severity you chose.
- Deadlines inside 30 days and matters with no activity for 30 days surface on
  the dashboard under **Needs attention**.

chunks.title: How CaseWize works
chunks.text:
Everything belongs to a firm: matters, documents, people, retention, billing.
You can hold a seat at more than one firm — the workspace switcher at the top of
the sidebar moves between them, and nothing is shared across the boundary.

Opening a new firm makes you its owner. Until a bar number is recorded on your
account you cannot approve AI output or release anything, whatever your role
says.

chunks.title: How CaseWize works
chunks.section: A matter is the unit of work
chunks.text:
A matter — the product also calls it a case — carries an internal number unique
to your firm, a court number once one exists, a matter type, a jurisdiction, a
phase, and two fields it cannot go active without: a **statute deadline** and a
**lead attorney**.

Inside a matter, work is split across tabs:

| Tab | What lives there |
| --- | --- |
| Overview | Strength, open alerts, next actions, recent developments |
| Parties | Who is involved, and the conflict check they trigger |
| Documents | The case file — everything filed on the matter |
| Analysis | Scores, developments, gaps, contradictions, actions, the memo |
| Chronology | Every dated event the documents produced, in order |
| Tasks | The board for this matter |
| Messages | Case-team threads and the client channel |
| Team | Who is on the matter, outside grants, ethical walls |
| Client | What has been released, and the client's accounts |
| Settings | The matter's own fields, status and retention |

chunks.title: How CaseWize works
chunks.text:
Your **firm role** decides what you are capable of. Your **case assignment**
decides whether a matter exists for you at all. The effective answer is the
intersection, minus any ethical wall — and a wall always wins.

A matter you are not on is not hidden from you in a list. It is absent from the
list, the counts and the search alike.

  A firm administrator is the clearest illustration: they run the roster and the
  billing, so they can see that a matter exists and manage who is on it, and
  they cannot open the file. That is deliberate, and no setting changes it.

chunks.title: How CaseWize works
chunks.section: The analysis reads the file, not your notes
chunks.text:
When a document is filed it is read in the background — the text is extracted
with its page numbers intact, so anything the analysis says can be traced to a
page. An analysis run then works through the file in stages and writes a new
version: a case summary, the legal research, a theory and damages model, a set
of scores, a memo, and the developments since last time.

Privileged and work-product documents are excluded from all of it. So are
documents that have been withdrawn, and documents recorded on the matter with no
file behind them.

chunks.title: How CaseWize works
chunks.section: Nothing the engine writes is final
chunks.text:
Every finding can be approved, rejected, marked incorrect or suppressed. Scores
can be overridden with a reason. Chronology rows can be corrected, struck or
frozen, and a row you touch stops being the engine's. Facts you record are
handed to every later run.

chunks.title: How CaseWize works
chunks.text:
- [Your first matter](/start/first-matter) walks the whole path once.
- [Roles and what they reach](/start/roles) is the permission reference.
- [How the analysis works](/analysis) explains runs, stages and versions.

chunks.title: Roles and what they reach
chunks.text:
A firm role is a **ceiling**. It says what you are capable of once you are on a
matter. It never puts you on one.

The live version of this table is in **Firm Settings → Roles & access**, which
also shows it for your firm's own configuration.

chunks.title: Roles and what they reach
chunks.text:
| Role | In one line |
| --- | --- |
| **Firm owner** | Billing, the plan, the firm itself, and the only role that can lift a legal hold. |
| **Firm admin** | Users, invitations, assignments and configuration — and no automatic access to any case file. |
| **Attorney** | Case work, plus sole authority to approve AI output. |
| **Paralegal** | Substantive case work. Drafts, never approves. |
| **Staff** | Upload, index, schedule. No AI run, no valuation, no client contact. |
| **Billing** | Invoices, usage and the plan. Case metadata only, never contents. |
| **External** | Nothing by default. Exists to receive a scoped, expiring grant to named documents. |
| **Client** | Portal only. Reads what has been released, never the case. |

chunks.title: Roles and what they reach
chunks.text:
| | Owner | Admin | Attorney | Paralegal | Staff | Billing |
| --- | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| Open a case file | ● | | ● | ● | ● | |
| Write to a case file | ● | | ● | ● | | |
| Create a matter | ● | | ● | | | |
| Add people to a matter | ● | ● | ● | | | |
| Advance the phase | ● | | ● | | | |
| Close a matter | ● | | ● | | | |
| Reopen a closed matter | ● | | | | | |
| Upload documents | ● | | ● | ● | ● | |
| Change a document's sensitivity flags | ● | | ● | | | |
| Run an analysis | ● | | ● | ● | | |
| Approve AI output | ● | | ● | | | |
| Release to the client | ● | | ● | | | |
| Set an ethical wall | ● | | ● | | | |
| Transfer the lead | ● | | ● | | | |
| Set a legal hold | ● | | ● | | | |
| Lift a legal hold | ● | | | | | |
| Invite and manage members | ● | ● | | | | |
| Read the audit log | ● | ● | ● | | | |
| Manage billing | ● | | | | | ● |

chunks.title: Roles and what they reach
chunks.section: Four things a tick above still does not give you
chunks.text:
**Being on the matter.** Every capability is conditional on an assignment. A
role never puts anyone on a case.

**Holding the lead.** Releasing to a client needs the lead attorney on that
specific matter — not any attorney on it, and not the firm owner unless they
hold the lead.

**A bar number on file.** Approving AI output is derived from licensure. It is
recorded on your account, never granted by an administrator.

**No wall on that matter.** An ethical wall is evaluated first and removes the
matter entirely, so a walled person fails every check identically to someone
simply not assigned.

chunks.title: Roles and what they reach
chunks.section: Two things outrank a role entirely
chunks.text:
**An ethical wall** is evaluated before anything else and beats every role,
  including the firm owner's. The walled person sees no trace — absent from
  lists, search, notifications, AI answers and counts. It is not a locked row.

  **A document's own flags.** Work product and privilege are hardcoded
  exclusions, not permission checkboxes. No role, no grant and no setting turns
  them on.

chunks.title: Roles and what they reach
chunks.section: Roles that are never invited from the People screen
chunks.text:
`client` and `external` are created through a matter, never through the org
chart. A client belongs to a matter; an outsider gets a scoped grant with an
expiry. Neither appears in a firm-wide user list, a search result or a team
picker.

chunks.title: Roles and what they reach
chunks.text:
`case: assign` without `case: read` is the whole point of the role. The office
manager runs the org chart, not the files. Opening a case detail gives them a
permission wall — they know it exists, they cannot read it.

A firm admin *may* assign themselves to a matter. Doing so notifies the firm
owner, and that notice is what stops "manages access" from quietly becoming "has
access".

chunks.title: Signing in
chunks.text:
You reach CaseWize one of four ways, and which one you took decides what you see.

**Invited by your firm.** A colleague with the right role sends an invitation to
your work email. The link expires in seven days, and joining through it verifies
your address. Your role is set on the invitation.

**You opened the firm.** Signing up directly makes you the firm owner of a new
firm, on a 30-day trial.

**Invited as a client.** A matter's lead attorney invites you to that matter's
portal. The invitation names the firm, never the matter. You get your own
account — never a shared login — and you see what has been released to you.

**Granted access as an outsider.** An expert or co-counsel is granted a named
set of documents on one matter, with an expiry date the field will not let
anyone leave blank.

chunks.title: Signing in
chunks.text:
A firm can require a second factor of every member. If yours does, nothing else
in the product opens until you have set one up — the requirement applies on your
next request, not at your next sign-in.

Setting it up: scan the code with any TOTP app (Google Authenticator,
1Password, Authy), save the backup codes somewhere that is not the phone you
just enrolled, then confirm with a code from the app. The first accepted code is
what switches it on.

- A code is not asked for on a device you marked as trusted, for thirty days.
- Backup codes work once each and are never shown again.
- Generating a new set invalidates the old set immediately.
- If your firm requires two-factor, you cannot turn it off yourself. An
  administrator can lift the firm requirement.

  If a code is rejected, check your phone's clock. Codes change every 30 seconds
  and a drifting clock is the usual cause. Too many failed codes locks the
  account for a short period.

chunks.title: Signing in
chunks.section: Being asked for your password again
chunks.text:
Some acts cannot be undone, and your firm can require your password again at the
moment of the act rather than trusting the session. The three it can cover:

- changing a colleague's role,
- deactivating a member,
- weakening the authentication policy itself.

Strengthening the policy never asks. See
[Authentication](/firm/authentication) for who configures this.

chunks.title: Signing in
chunks.text:
**Your account → Where you are signed in** lists every session, with the device
and when it started. Revoke any you do not recognise. Revoking takes effect on
that device's next request, not at its next sign-in.

Changing your password ends every other session immediately.

chunks.title: Signing in
chunks.text:
If you hold a seat at more than one firm, the workspace switcher at the top of
the sidebar moves between them. Each firm sets its own authentication
requirements, so another one may ask you to enrol too. Invitations waiting on
you appear in the same menu.

chunks.title: Signing in
chunks.text:
| Message | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| Your seat at this firm could not be confirmed | Your membership changed while you were signed in. Sign in again. |
| Seat suspended | An administrator deactivated your seat at that firm. |
| Too many attempts. Please wait a moment | Rate limiting. It clears on its own. |
| That password is not right | Step-up re-authentication failed; the act was not performed. |

chunks.title: Tasks
chunks.text:
| Source | |
| --- | --- |
| **Added by hand** | Somebody created it. |
| **From a template** | Raised by a rule. |
| **From intake** | Created when the matter was opened. |
| **From the analysis** | A recommended action somebody turned into a task. |

chunks.title: Tasks
chunks.text:
Title, detail, **kind** (filing, discovery, review, evidence, client, court,
internal), **priority** (low, normal, high, critical), assignee, **start** and
**due** dates, and **critical deadline**.

  A **critical deadline** pins the task to the top of every board in the firm
  and cannot be muted. It needs a date.

chunks.title: Tasks
chunks.text:
To do · In progress · **Blocked** · Done · Cancelled.

Marking a task blocked asks what it is blocked on, and that reason shows on the
task until it is unblocked.

chunks.title: Tasks
chunks.text:
A task can be **waiting on** other tasks and **blocking** others. The board
refuses to create a cycle, and refuses to close a task whose prerequisites are
still open.

The timeline layout draws the links and flags any that run backwards — *a
prerequisite is due after the work waiting on it*.

chunks.title: Tasks
chunks.text:
**Table** — sortable columns, bulk selection.

**Board** — kanban by status, drag between columns.

**Calendar** — by due date, month at a time. Tasks with no date are counted
below rather than dropped silently.

**Timeline** — bars from start to due, at day, week, month or quarter zoom. Drag
a bar to reschedule it, or its edges to change when the work starts and ends.

chunks.title: Tasks
chunks.text:
The built-in views: **My work**, **Board**, **Overdue**, **This week**,
**Unassigned**, **Calendar**, **Timeline**.

**Save view** keeps the filters, sort and layout exactly as they are on screen,
with a scope:

- **Just me** — nobody else sees it.
- **This matter** — everyone on the matter, on this matter's board only.
- **The firm** — everyone at the firm. They still only see their own work.

**Make default** decides which view opens first.

chunks.title: Tasks
chunks.text:
Group by any field. Filter to open only, overdue, or mine. Search by title.
Select rows to change status, priority or assignee in bulk, or to delete —
deleting takes the dependency links with it and cannot be undone.

  A board that says *showing the first 200* is truncated. Narrow the filters to
  get a complete answer rather than reading a partial one as the total.

chunks.title: Outside experts and co-counsel
chunks.text:
An outsider is not a member with fewer permissions. They are granted **named
documents on one matter**, with an expiry date.

chunks.title: Outside experts and co-counsel
chunks.text:
**Add to the matter → An outsider**.

- Pick someone who already holds an outside seat at the firm, or **invite a new
  one by email** — the seat and the grant are created together when they accept.
- Tick the documents the grant reaches. A grant is to named documents, never to
  the matter. At least one is required.
- Set an **expiry date**. The field will not take a blank.

Work product and privileged documents are never in that list, whatever anyone
ticks.

chunks.title: Outside experts and co-counsel
chunks.text:
Regardless of which documents you name, an external grant never reaches:

- Work product
- Risk and settlement figures
- Attorney notes
- Client communications
- Fees and billing
- Unreviewed AI output
- Any other matter

chunks.title: Outside experts and co-counsel
chunks.text:
Access dies on the date whether or not anyone remembers. The lead is reminded
  seven days out — that reminder is a courtesy; the date is the control.

**Revoke this grant** ends it early.

chunks.title: Outside experts and co-counsel
chunks.text:
They do not get the product. They get **Shared with you**: the matters they have
been given documents on, the documents themselves, and when the access ends.

The page says so plainly — *you see only what was shared, and only until the
access ends* — and each matter carries a *named documents only* badge.

chunks.title: Outside experts and co-counsel
chunks.text:
**Firm Settings → People** has an *External access, across every matter* panel
listing every outstanding grant, how many documents each reaches, and which are
expiring. Grants are created from the matter, never from there.

chunks.title: The case team
chunks.text:
The **Team** tab is the access list for one matter: firm members on it, external
grants, client accounts, ethical walls — and, deliberately, everyone at the firm
who is *not* on it.

chunks.title: The case team
chunks.text:
A firm role sets the ceiling. The assignment decides whether it applies here at
all. There is no separate role to pick when you add someone: their firm role
decides what they can do once inside.

Each person on the roster shows what their assignment actually carries:

- Reads the file
- Writes to the file
- Approves AI output
- Releases to the client
- Manages the roster

chunks.title: The case team
chunks.text:
**Add to the matter → A colleague**. Pick the person, optionally record why
(*second-chairing the depositions*), and add them.

The conflict check runs against the firm's parties before anyone is added, and
the lead attorney is notified either way — **including when a firm owner or
administrator adds themselves**. That notice is what stops "manages access" from
quietly becoming "has access".

If nobody is left to add, everyone eligible is already on the matter or walled
off from it.

chunks.title: The case team
chunks.text:
**Remove from the matter**. Access ends on their **next request**, not at their
next sign-in.

  Removing someone does not remove what they did. Their name stays on every
  entry, approval and audit line they created, with the role they held at the
  time.

chunks.title: The case team
chunks.text:
The interesting half of an access list. It counts the firm members with **no
access row** at all — for whom this matter does not appear in any list, count or
search.

Administering the firm is not the same as being on a matter, and this panel is
where that becomes visible.

An ethical wall is a different thing again: a deny that beats every role, lifted
by a recorded waiver rather than by adding somebody back. See [Ethical
walls](/team/walls).

chunks.title: The lead attorney
chunks.section: What the lead alone can do
chunks.text:
**Release to the client.** Not any attorney on the matter, and not the firm
owner unless they hold the lead. Releasing and revoking on a matter belong to
its lead alone.

**Open a client thread to the client.** A client channel is created shut; the
lead opens it.

The lead is also who gets notified when someone is added to the matter, and who
is reminded seven days before an external grant expires.

chunks.title: The lead attorney
chunks.text:
Only members who hold a **bar number** on file. The same licence is what grants
the right to approve AI output.

If you are not in the list, record your bar number and the state that issued it
on [Your account](/account).

chunks.title: The lead attorney
chunks.text:
**Transfer the lead** on the Team tab. Pick the new lead, then decide what
happens to the outgoing one:

- **Stays on the matter** — keeps their assignment and everything it carries,
  minus the release right.
- **Comes off the matter** — access ends on their next request, not at their next
  sign-in.

  The transfer is atomic: never zero leads, never two. The Settings tab shows
  the lead but will not change it — handing a matter over happens on the Team
  tab, by the outgoing lead or the firm owner.

If nobody else on the matter holds a bar number, add an attorney to the roster
first.

chunks.title: The lead attorney
chunks.section: A matter cannot be left without one
chunks.text:
Two rules follow from that:

- You cannot remove the lead from a matter. Transfer it first.
- A firm member who still leads at least one matter cannot be deactivated. *A
  case cannot be left without a lead attorney, even for an afternoon.*

chunks.title: Ethical walls
chunks.text:
The walled person sees **no trace** of the matter — not in lists, search,
  notifications, AI answers or counts. It beats every role, including the firm
  owner's.

It is evaluated before anything else, which means a walled person fails every
check identically to someone who was simply never assigned. There is no locked
row, no greyed-out entry, nothing to notice.

chunks.title: Ethical walls
chunks.text:
They are not the same.

- **Absence from the roster** means no access row. The matter does not appear
  for that person.
- **A wall** is an active deny. It survives being added to the matter, and it
  beats a firm role that would otherwise reach the file.

That is why the Team tab lists them separately, and why lifting a wall is not
the same as adding somebody back.

chunks.title: Ethical walls
chunks.text:
**Wall someone off** on the Team tab. Pick the person and type a **reason —
kept permanently**: why must this person not see the matter?

Attorneys and the firm owner can set a wall.

chunks.title: Ethical walls
chunks.text:
**Lift the wall**, with a reason kept permanently. It is recorded as a
**waiver, never a deletion** — the fact that a wall existed survives, with who
set it, who lifted it, and both reasons.

chunks.title: Ethical walls
chunks.text:
- The matter's **Team** tab, active and lifted.
- **Firm Settings → People**, across every matter, as *person — matter*.

They are not listed on your own account. A walled matter shows no trace
anywhere, and a line saying you are walled off one would be the disclosure the
wall exists to prevent.

chunks.title: Ethical walls
chunks.text:
A conflict check runs as the system, so it sees walled matters. It reports that
something matched and who it matched — and nothing else. The matter is not
named, and nobody on it is named.
